recipes.name: Grandma Kay's Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package shredded Colby-Monterey Jack cheese
0.5 (4 ounce) can chopped green chile peppers, drained
2 (10.75 ounce) cans cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 11x15-inch baking dish with nonstick spray.

Place chicken breasts in a large saucepan with enough water to barely cover; bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until chicken is no longer pink in the center, about 15 minutes. Remove from the saucepan, drain, and shred with 2 forks.
Place shredded chicken into a large bowl. Add 1 (8-ounce) package Colby-Monterey Jack cheese and canned green chilies. Mix well.

Spoon about 3 tablespoons chicken mixture in a line down the center of each tortilla and fold tortilla in half, enclosing filling. Starting at the filled side, roll the folded tortilla into a cylinder. Place each enchilada, seam-side down, into the prepared baking dish.

Whisk together condensed soup, half-and-half, chicken broth, and about 1/3 of the remaining Colby-Monterey Jack cheese package in another large bowl until well combined. Pour over enchiladas, then sprinkle remaining Colby-Monterey Jack cheese over the top. Let stand for 10 to 15 minutes.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and cheese topping is melted and beginning to brown, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma Kay's Chicken Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: This chicken enchiladas recipe is a Mexican-inspired casserole of meat-stuffed flour tortillas covered with a mild, creamy chile sauce and cheese.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful recipe! I have 8 kids and even the pickiest loved this recipe!!! The only thing I'd do differently is double the sauce but only because I used 2 smaller pan...

I have made this recipe twice now and we love it! I added refried beans to the tortilla along with the filling and put half the can of chilies in the filling and the other half in the sauce that is poured over the enchiladas. This recipe is so yummy!
I love to use a rotisserie chicken to speed up the process.

Great recipe! I assembled everything 3 days before I baked it, and it turned out perfect. I baked it at 375 degrees for 35 minutes straight out of the frig. I also added more green chili peppers to the sauce for a little more flavor. Everyone in my house loved it!

Very easy recipe, but was bland. I'll make this again and add fajita seasoning to the chicken cheese mixture. Also I cut the recipe down since it's the two of us.
I made this a second time using a packet of fajita seasoning , turned out GREAT! Husband loved it.

I used to make this a lot when our family had weekly Sunday dinners. I’ve seen the comments about being “mushy” and bland but mine have never turned out mushy. I think I’ve had success bc: 1. I boil my chicken in water that has onions, celery, carrots, sage, poultry seasoning, minced garlic, 2. I use a container of sour cream to the sauce/filling, along with Quesadilla cheese and the Colby Jack. My chicken is always very flavorful.
Delicious! I put the oven on broil for only a few minutes before taking it out of the oven which crisped it up nicely.

I've made this recipe what seems like a million times. It's always a hit, no matter where I take it! 
I have made a couple changes along the way, which in my opinion, makes this recipe ten times better. I don't use the green chile peppers, instead, I substitute those with hot sauce inside the enchiladas.
Also, I've found that if you let the sauce sit as long as the recipe suggests, the tortillas get soggy, and nobody likes soggy food!
And, as much as I love cheese, I think this recipe uses way too much of it. I probably use 1 full package of cheese in the whole recipe instead of the two full bags it recommends. 

However, with all of my little tweaks, this recipe is SUPERB.

Delicious! My husband loved it. Creamy and Cheesy. I used leftover chicken tenders and extra slices of Monterey jack cheese on the tortilla when layering. Wow! Will be making this again. Thanks for sharing this recipe Grandma Kay!

These were delicious. I pureed the chiles just for personal preference. I also mixed some chiles, salt and pepper in the topping for extra flavor. It made 14 large ones and between 4 of us only 1 was left!

I took others advice and I increased the sauce by 1/2 and it was about right. This makes a whole lot! Unless I’m feeding a crowd I will divide it in half next time. I thought the amount of cheese was about right as well. It needs more spice so next time I will add jalapeños, onions and maybe some garlic, cayenne pepper, and chili powder to the chicken mixture.
We make the sauce from cream of chicken soup and chopped green chilis! We also cook the chicken in chicken broth with some bullion and poultry seasoning in it!

I added a few things but otherwise followed the recipe as is and hubby had four helpings! I used some green verde sauce throughout as we love the flavor. I did season the chicken with taco seasoning and used cheddar as that is what we had on hand. It was very good and very easy. Will definately do again.
Not as tasteful as I was hoping for. Also, I agree with the mushy texture, which I couldn't get past. Would definitely add more spices and less liquid next time.

I made this as the instructions said but it turned out soggy. The tortillas were mushy, a little bit slimy and didn't hold their shape. Too much sauce. It tasted good tho. If I make this again, I will decrease the liquid amounts.
I really liked this recipe very easy to make. Will be making this again very soon
Enjoyed the Enchiladas...was great with all the condiment I had.
Turned out perfect! Thank you so much!
